title: 社会シミュレーション
subtitle: Social Simulation
keywords: Social Systems 2.Mathematical Models 3.Monte Carlo Method 4.Agents 5.System Dynamics
educationalGoal: In this course, students learn about mathematical modeling of social systems and simulation techniques. Students understand system dynamics and multi-agent models—representative mathematical models that incorporate interactions among people or between humans and the natural environment. Students also understand to acquire insights into the macroscopic characteristics and global behavior of economic, social, and environmental systems through simulations using these models.
advice: In this course, students study "systems thinking", which means an approach that focuses on the interactions among components of a system considered as a whole system. Students learn the basics of mathematical modeling and perform simulations using these models. Students break down a complex system into its components, analyze causal relationships, and use these relationships to understand changes in outcomes based on different parameter settings via simulation. Through simulation, students grasp real-world social phenomena and trends, forecast future conditions, and clarify what actions are necessary for building a better society. Advice for Students is as follows: 1. Maintain a habit of considering relationships among various things in daily life. 2. If you cannot understand something at once, ask questions and review the material. 3. Engage in hands-on simulation practice, and reflect critically on the results, for example, "Does this match what I expected?", "How should I interpret this result?”
books: Textbook: None Reference Books: None Reserved Books: None
requiredKnowledge: This course is designed so that no special prior knowledge is required. However, familiarity with computers is desirable. Basic mathematical knowledge, such as differential equations and linear algebra, will deepen your understanding of mathematical models and simulation techniques. Reference materials for mathematics will be introduced during class as needed.

activityGoals.body: Understand mathematical models involving population and competition dynamics .
Implement simple mathematical models as simulation models.
Understand and perform simulations using system dynamics and multi-agent approaches.
Execute simulations, organize results, and create visualizations.
Consider methods for verifying simulation results.

achievementLevels.ideal: Students can derive mathematical models even for complex systems, implement simulation models, conduct parametric simulations, and explain parameter effects appropriately. They can also explain fundamental concepts of system dynamics and organize the effects of parameters.
achievementLevels.standard: Students can derive mathematical models for systems with few components and simple relationships, implement simulations, and organize results. They also understand basic concepts of system dynamics.

lessons.content: Guidance: What is Social Simulation? Course overview, evaluation methods Registration for Insight Maker (system dynamics tool) Registration for Artisoc Cloud (multi-agent simulator)
Modeling and abstraction of social phenomena -Assumptions, variables, parameters -Population dynamics simulation
Foundations of decision-making models -Perfect rationality and bounded rationality -Utility, cost, and reward -Decision-making over time -Differences between "optimization" and "simulation"
Introduction to System Dynamics (1) -Flow and stock -Temporal evolution -Competition simulation
Introduction to System Dynamics (2) -Infectious disease spread simulation -Mechanisms of infection expansion -Effects of policy interventions (quarantine, vaccines)
Complex systems and emergent phenomena -Individual behavior and collective phenomena -Emergence and self-organization -Nonlinearity and prediction difficulty
Cellular Automata (CA) -Basic structure of CA -Rules and temporal evolution -Applications to social phenomena: fire spread -Analysis of the Game of Life
Introduction to Agent-Based Models (ABM) -Agents, environment, interactions -Differences from CA -Advantages of ABM in social simulation
Famous ABM models -Schelling’s segregation model: model structure, unintended consequences, policy implications and limitations -Competition simulation: differences from system dynamics
Learning and evolving agents -Fixed rules vs. optimization vs. learning -Relationship between dynamic programming (DP) and reinforcement learning -Modeling social evolution
Networks and social structure -Basics of social networks -Diffusion of information, rumors, and infections -Influence of network structure on decision-making
Urban, transportation, and evacuation simulation -Spatial models -Bottlenecks and congestion -DP-based route choice vs. local rules
Economic and market simulation -Artificial markets -Bubbles and crashes -Optimal behavior and collective instability
Verification, validity, and ethics -Validation and sensitivity analysis -Relationship with real data -Policy applications and ethical issues
